ledPatterns.pattern: IGC (integrated gas control) LED ON steady
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation.
Hardware failure — no power to the IGC or failed board.
checks: Check 24 V to the IGC and its fuse; replace IGC if powered and dark (field practice)

ledPatterns.meaning: Fan ON/OFF delay modified.
checks: Informational: the fan delay jumper/setting has been changed from default

ledPatterns.meaning: Limit switch fault — high-temperature limit switch is open.
checks: Check indoor airflow (filters, belt, blower), limit switch continuity, and heat exchanger temperature rise (field practice)

ledPatterns.meaning: Flame sense fault — the IGC sensed flame that should not be present.
checks: Check for a leaking/stuck gas valve, flame sensor shorted to ground, or wiring; reset at the unit disconnect (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: 4 consecutive limit switch faults — inadequate airflow to the unit.
checks: Correct airflow (filters, belt, motor, dampers) then reset power (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Ignition lockout fault — the unit unsuccessfully attempted ignition for 15 minutes.
checks: Check gas supply and pressure, igniter, flame sensor, gas valve; reset at the unit disconnect (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Induced-draft motor fault — the IGC does not sense that the induced-draft motor is operating.
checks: Check IDM operation and the speed/hall-effect feedback wiring to the IGC (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Rollout switch fault — the rollout switch has opened. The rollout switch will automatically reset, but the IGC will continue to lock out the unit; reset at the unit disconnect.
checks: Find the cause of flame rollout (blocked heat exchanger/flue, low airflow, burner problems) before resetting (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Internal control fault — the microprocessor has sensed an error in the software or hardware.
checks: Cycle power; replace the IGC if it repeats (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Main Base Board processor running; the red LED on each board should blink in sync with the others, with the MBB as the lead board.
checks: If blinking is absent or asynchronous suspect a board communication issue: disconnect the LEN/CCN plugs and check resistance on the communication lines; check LEN connections at J3/J4 (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Local Equipment Network active — should always be blinking whenever power is on.
checks: If not blinking check board power and LEN wiring; a lost LEN can generate A152 (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Carrier Comfort Network communication in progress — blinks only while CCN traffic is present.
checks: Steady off with a BAS connected: check CCN bus wiring, address and baud rate (field practice)

controls.name: EconoMi$er X (Honeywell W7220 JADE) economizer controller
controls.description: Factory-installed option on 48/50TC/HC/LC/FC/GC/KC/JC/FE and Bryant/ICP equivalents from ~2013 (replaces EconoMi$er IV). 2-line LCD with 4-button navigation; ALARMS(n) menu shows active alarms only, with n = number of active alarms. Sensors: S-bus digital sensors (OAT/RAT enthalpy) plus 20K mixed-air (MAT) and optional CO2 / DA. Alarm strings are transcribed from the Honeywell JADE W7220 installation instructions 63-2700 / 62-0331, which Carrier reproduces in the EconoMi$er X IIK-CRECOMZR instructions and 48TC/50TC IOMs. Early-firmware modules show ACT UNDER V / ACT OVER V / ACT STALLED and SYS ALARM; later firmware (63-2700-11) consolidates the actuator faults into ACT ERROR and adds OA SENS T ERR, FREEZE ALARM, SHUTDOWN ACTIVE, DMP CAL RUNNING and DA SENS ALM. Both sets are included so the assistant matches whatever the LCD shows; coverage is complete for the 63-2700-11 alarm list. Confidence is left at low pending an independent verifier reading of the Honeywell alarm page (the strings were verified by search summary only).

faultCodes.meaning: Alarms are displayed only while active; the ALARMS menu title shows the count in parentheses. Which alarms can appear depends on the configured sensors (e.g. CO2 alarms only with a DCV sensor).
likelyCauses: Sensor open/short/out of range (MAT, OAT, RAT, CO2, SAT)
Actuator over-/under-voltage, stall or communication error
checks: Press the down arrow from the home screen to ALARMS; press ENTER to view each alarm and its description
Correct the sensor/actuator issue; alarms clear automatically when the condition is gone
faultCodes.source: Carrier EconoMi$er X (Honeywell W7220) Installation, Setup and Troubleshooting (manualslib 2855215); Carrier IIK-CRECOMZR67-03 Low-Leak EconoMi$er X Installation Instructions — 'Alarms' table — 'Alarms' (menu behaviour; individual alarm strings follow, transcribed from Honeywell 63-2700 / 62-0331)

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): mixed air sensor has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: MAT sensor (20K NTC) open, shorted or unplugged at the MAT / MAT T1 terminals
Sensor lead damaged; sensor fell out of the mixed-air stream
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: ohm the sensor (20K at 77 °F) at the module terminals; compare the STATUS menu MA TEMP reading to a reference thermometer
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'MAT SENS ERR: Indicates that the mixed air sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check wiring and replace sensor if alarm persists.'
faultCodes.notes: Displayed on the W7220 LCD ALARMS (#) menu; the economizer then runs with damper at minimum position and mechanical cooling only.

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): CO2 sensor has failed, gone out of range, or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: CO2 (IAQ) sensor unpowered, miswired at IAQ 2-10 / IAQ COM / IAQ 24V, or output out of the 2–10 V range
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: measure the IAQ 2-10 V signal at the module; confirm 24 VAC to the sensor; if DCV is not used, set DCV to NONE in SETUP so the alarm does not occur
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'CO2 SENS ERR: Indicates that the CO2 sensor has failed, gone out of range, or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): outdoor air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor temperature reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: C7400A enthalpy sensor (or C7250A temperature sensor) on the S-BUS unplugged, wired backwards is not an issue (polarity-insensitive) but open/shorted S-BUS lead is
Sensor failed; more than the supported number of Sylk devices on the bus
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: verify the S-BUS pair is intact and the sensor is set to OA (jumper/DIP per sensor instructions); check the STATUS menu for the OA sensor readings
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'OA SYLK T ERR / OA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the outdoor air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): outdoor air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor humidity reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: C7400A enthalpy sensor humidity element failed or sensor disconnected from the S-BUS
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: compare OA HUM in the STATUS menu with a sling psychrometer; replace the sensor if far off or missing
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'OA SYLK T ERR / OA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the outdoor air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): return air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor temperature reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Return-air C7400A sensor disconnected from the S-BUS or failed
Sensor addressed as OA instead of RA (two sensors with the same address)
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: only fitted on differential-enthalpy configurations — verify S-BUS wiring and the RA address setting on the sensor
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'RA SYLK T ERR / RA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the return air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): return air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor humidity reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Return-air C7400A humidity element failed or sensor disconnected
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'RA SYLK T ERR / RA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the return air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): discharge air (Sylk-bus) sensor has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: C7250A discharge-air sensor unplugged from the S-BUS or failed
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: the DA sensor is optional — if not installed, make sure the module is not configured to expect one
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'DA SYLK T ERR: Indicates that the discharge air sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, newer firmware): outdoor air temperature sensor (20K wired OAT input) has failed or become disconnected — 'SENS T' is shown instead of 'SYLK T' when a 20K OA temperature sensor is used.
likelyCauses: 20K OAT sensor open/shorted or unplugged at the OAT / OAT T1 terminals
Sensor lead damaged by the condenser fan or weather
checks: Manual (by analogy with the other sensor rows): check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: ohm the sensor at the module (20K at 77 °F) and compare OA TEMP in the STATUS menu to ambient
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' menu list ('OA SENS T ERR'; 'When using 20k OA temperature sensors, SENS T will appear on the screen')

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, newer firmware): the actuator has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Damper actuator stalled (damper jammed, linkage bound, ice or debris)
Actuator supply voltage out of range (below 21.6 V or above 26.4 V) at ACT 24V / ACT COM
Actuator unplugged from ACT 2-10 / S-BUS, or actuator failed
checks: Manual: check for stall, over voltage, under voltage and actuator count; replace the actuator if the damper is movable and the supply voltage is between 21.6 V and 26.4 V
Field practice: run CHECKOUT > DAMPER OPEN / DAMPER CLOSE and watch the damper travel; free a bound damper before condemning the actuator
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'ACT ERROR: Indicates that the actuator has failed or become disconnected. Check for stall, over voltage, under voltage and actuator count. Replace the actuator if damper is movable and supply voltage is between 21.6 V and 26.4 V.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, earlier firmware): voltage received by the actuator is below the expected range.
likelyCauses: Low 24 VAC supply to the actuator (undersized/overloaded transformer, long thin wiring, poor connection at ACT 24V / ACT COM)
checks: Field practice: measure 24 VAC at the actuator power terminals under load; must be within 21.6–26.4 V (per the ACT ERROR row); correct the supply or connections
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'ACT UNDER V: Indicates voltage received by the actuator is below the expected range.' (manualsdir 131876 p.19)

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, earlier firmware): voltage received by the actuator is above the expected range.
likelyCauses: High control-transformer secondary (wrong primary tap for line voltage), or actuator miswired
checks: Field practice: measure actuator supply; if above 26.4 V check the transformer primary tap and line voltage
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'ACT OVER V: Indicates voltage received by the actuator is above the expected range.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, earlier firmware): the actuator stopped before achieving its commanded position.
likelyCauses: Damper blades or linkage binding, ice/debris in the hood, actuator clutch slipping
Actuator stroke or rotation direction set wrong
checks: Field practice: disengage the actuator clutch and move the damper by hand through full travel; run CHECKOUT DAMPER OPEN/CLOSE and confirm the damper reaches both ends
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'ACT STALLED: Indicates the actuator stopped before achieving its commanded position.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): outdoor temperature is below the LOW TEMP LOCKOUT setting or the mixed air temperature is below the Lo setpoint; the alarm clears when conditions return to the normal range.
likelyCauses: Genuinely cold outdoor air with the damper open (freeze protection is doing its job)
MAT sensor reading low (misplaced in a cold stream) or LOW TEMP LOCKOUT / MAT LO SET configured too high
checks: Manual: alarm self-clears when temperatures return to normal range
Field practice: confirm the damper drives closed on the freeze alarm; verify MAT sensor placement and the SETUP values MAT LO SET / LOW T LOCK
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'FREEZE ALARM: Indicates that the outdoor temperature is below the LOW Temp Lockout setting or the mixed air temperature is below the Lo Setpoint. The alarm will clear when conditions return to normal range.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): AUX2 IN is programmed for SHUTDOWN and 24 V has been applied to the AUX2 IN terminal.
likelyCauses: Smoke detector / fire alarm or BAS shutdown input is energizing AUX2 IN (intended)
AUX2 IN mis-programmed as SHUTDOWN while wired for another function (e.g. occupancy or HEAT input)
checks: Field practice: confirm what is feeding 24 V to AUX2 IN; if the input is meant to be occupancy/heat, change AUX2 IN in the SETUP menu
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'SHUTDOWN ACTIVE: Indicates that AUX2 IN is programmed for SHUTDOWN and 24 V has been applied to the AUX 2IN terminal.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): DCV Auto enable has been programmed and the JADE is completing a calibration on the dampers.
likelyCauses: Normal — automatic damper calibration in progress after power-up or a configuration change
checks: Field practice: wait for the calibration to finish before judging damper position or running CHECKOUT
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'DMP CAL RUNNING: Displays if DCV Auto enable has been programmed and the Jade is completing a calibration on the dampers.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): the discharge air temperature is out of the range set in the ADVANCED SETUP menu.
likelyCauses: Discharge air too cold/hot relative to the DA LO/HI alarm limits (mechanical cooling or heat problem, or damper stuck open in cold weather)
DA sensor reading wrong or alarm limits set too tight
checks: Field practice: compare DA TEMP in STATUS with a duct thermometer; review ADVANCED SETUP discharge-air alarm limits; check the unit's cooling/heating operation
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'DA SENS ALM: Indicates that the discharge air temperature is out of the range set in the ADVANCED SETUP Menu.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): when AUX1-O is set to SYS and any alarm exists (e.g. failed sensors), the AUX1-O terminal has 24 VAC out (system alarm output).
likelyCauses: Any other active JADE alarm — this is the summary output, not a fault by itself
checks: Field practice: open the ALARMS (#) menu and clear the underlying alarm(s); AUX1-O drops out when no alarms remain
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'SYS ALARM: When AUX1-O is set to SYS and there is any alarm (e.g., failed sensors), the AUX1-O terminal has 24 Vac out.' (manualsdir 131876 p.19)

diagnosticTips: Home screen shows status; press the down arrow to scroll STATUS, SETPOINTS, SYSTEM SETUP, ADVANCED SETUP, CHECKOUT, ALARMS(n). ENTER edits; up/down change values.
CHECKOUT menu drives the damper (open / closed / minimum) and exercises outputs for testing without a thermostat call.
Verify OAT and RAT sensors are recognised (SYSTEM SETUP > sensors); a missing OAT sensor disables free cooling entirely.

EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE) interface: 2-line 16-character LCD with a 4-button keypad (Menu Up, Menu Down, Enter, Exit) mounted in the economizer/control box. Menus: STATUS, SETUP, ADVANCED SETUP, CHECKOUT, ALARMS(#). Alarms show only while active.

EconoMi$er X clearing an alarm: navigate to the alarm in ALARMS, press Enter — 'ERASE?' displays — press Enter again; 'ALARM ERASED' confirms; press Menu Up/Exit to return. If the condition still exists the alarm re-displays within 5 seconds.

EconoMi$er X power-up: the JADE waits 60 minutes after power-up before checking for alarms; a sensor that loses communication after being detected shows a device-fail error, and after 60 minutes the module drops to operation mode with the missing device alarmed.

EconoMi$er X checkout: CHECKOUT menu tests DAMPER MINIMUM (drives to configured minimum), DAMPER OPEN (fully open; exhaust-fan contacts energize during this test) and DAMPER CLOSE (fully closed) — use them to prove actuator/damper travel when ACT ERROR / ACT STALLED is shown. The controller must see Y1-G / occupancy inputs per the SETUP for normal economizing.

controls.name: EconoMi$er IV / EconoMi$er2 (Honeywell W7212 analog economizer controller)
controls.description: Analog economizer controller used on 48/50TC/HC and legacy 48/50HJ/TJ (2003-~2014). No fault codes: diagnosis is by the three LEDs (Free Cool, DCV, Exhaust) and terminal voltages. EconoMi$er2 is the same damper package driven by a DDC controller (PremierLink / ComfortLink / RTU Open) via 4-20 mA instead of the W7212.

faultCodes.meaning: The W7212 has no displayed fault codes. Free Cool LED on = outdoor air suitable (economizing enabled); DCV LED on = demand-control-ventilation active (CO2 above setpoint); Exhaust LED on = power exhaust output energized.
likelyCauses: Damper not moving: no 24 VAC at TR/TR1, actuator failure, enthalpy sensor (C7400) failed
Free Cool LED never lights: enthalpy setpoint too low, outdoor enthalpy sensor open, jumper/DIP configuration
Damper stuck open in occupied: minimum-position pot set high, or 2-10 VDC signal fault
checks: Measure 24 VAC between TR and TR1
Measure 2-10 VDC at the actuator (P/P1 minimum position pot); 2 V = closed, 10 V = open
Simulate a low outdoor enthalpy: jumper SO/+ per the IOM checkout table and confirm Free Cool LED and damper open
Check the C7400 enthalpy sensor at SO/+ (should read ~3-25 mA depending on enthalpy)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48/50TC Installation Instructions — 'EconoMi$er IV' / 'EconoMi$er2' sections and W7212 troubleshooting table
faultCodes.notes: From memory of the 48TC IOM economizer checkout; verify in the unit's installation instructions.

ledPatterns.meaning: Outdoor air is suitable for free cooling (enthalpy/dry-bulb changeover satisfied); the damper modulates on a cooling call.
checks: Checkout (Honeywell 63-2596 / Carrier IIK-CRECOMZR52): with the 620-ohm checkout resistor across SO and + and the enthalpy pot at A, the Free Cool LED turns on and the actuator drives to about 45° open (DCV Max at mid position); turning the pot to D (fully CW) or removing the resistor turns the LED off and drives the actuator fully closed

ledPatterns.meaning: The module is in demand-controlled ventilation (CO2) mode and is overriding the minimum position.
checks: Verify the CO2 sensor 2-10 V signal and the DCV Set/DCV Max pot settings

ledPatterns.meaning: The exhaust-fan contact (EXH1/EXH2) is closed — damper position has exceeded the Exhaust Fan Set Point.
checks: Adjust the Exh Fan Set pot if the power exhaust runs too early/late

ledPatterns.meaning: No 24 VAC to the module (TR/TR1) or the module has failed; the W7212 has no fault-code display — diagnosis is by LED state plus the checkout table.
checks: Thermostat/unit signals at Y1, G, O and the 2-10 V actuator output

diagnosticTips: The W7212 is mounted on the economizer damper assembly or in the control box; potentiometers set minimum position, DCV max, exhaust setpoint and the enthalpy changeover (A/B/C/D or 1-6 on later units).
With the W7212 removed from a unit with a DDC controller (PremierLink/RTU Open/SystemVu), the damper is driven directly by the controller (EconoMi$er2) — do not look for the W7212.
Frozen evaporator or high humidity with the unit off often traces to a damper that fails to close (spring-return actuator failure or minimum position set too high).

EconoMi$er IV (W7212 logic module) has no display and no alarm codes: diagnose with the three LEDs (Free Cool, DCV, Exh), the potentiometer settings and the Honeywell checkout table (620-ohm resistor across SO and +, enthalpy pot A vs D, DCV Max mid) — see ledPatterns.
EconoMi$er 2 is the simpler DCV-capable economizer without a logic-module display; it also has no fault codes — verify by 24 V inputs, actuator 2-10 V and damper travel.

controls.name: Carrier PremierLink rooftop controller
controls.description: Carrier CCN-compatible DDC controller (2000s-2010s) fitted to 48/50HJ/TJ/TC/HC as the '1' base-unit-controls option; communicates on the CCN bus and works with a T-55/T-56 space sensor. Alarms are read with a Navigator/System Pilot or ComfortVIEW/i-Vu via CCN.

faultCodes.meaning: PremierLink reports sensor failures (space, supply-air, outdoor-air), fan/compressor status failures, fire/smoke shutdown, dirty filter and IAQ alarms as text alarms on the CCN bus. No local flash-code table.
likelyCauses: Fan status switch / compressor safety open
checks: Connect a Navigator or System Pilot to the CCN port (or use i-Vu/ComfortVIEW) and read Alarms; check the input named in the alarm
faultCodes.source: Carrier PremierLink Controller Installation, Start-Up and Configuration Instructions — alarm/status section (from memory; verify)

diagnosticTips: PremierLink has status LEDs on the board (power, communication) and a service-test capability through the Navigator SERVICE TEST menu; refer to the PremierLink installation instructions for the LED meanings.
PremierLink was superseded by RTU Open (multi-protocol) around 2010-2012 and by SystemVu later; many PremierLink boards have been replaced in the field with RTU Open kits.

controls.name: Electromechanical controls with conventional thermostat (no unit controller)
controls.description: Base-unit-controls option 0 on 48/50TC/HC/FC/GC/KC and all legacy 48/50HJ/TJ/TM/TF and 38AU/40RU splits: relays, contactors, CLO/compressor lockout board, IGC for gas heat, driven by a 24 V thermostat (R, C, G, Y1, Y2, W1, W2). Faults are found by tracing 24 V through the safety strings; the only 'codes' are the IGC LED (gas units) and the CLO / phase-monitor LEDs.

faultCodes.meaning: The compressor lockout (CLO) relay/board has opened the compressor circuit after a safety (HPS, LPS, freeze stat) opened during a call; it latches until the thermostat call is removed (Y) or control power is cycled.
likelyCauses: LPS trip (low charge, low airflow / iced coil, low ambient)
checks: Check 24 V across each safety in the string (HPS, LPS, FPT) with the call active; the open one drops the 24 V
Reset by removing the Y call at the thermostat (or cycling the disconnect); if it retrips, diagnose the pressure condition with gauges
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48/50TC Installation Instructions — 'Compressor Lockout' / troubleshooting section (from memory; verify)

faultCodes.meaning: Phase monitor relay (PMR) has dropped out for phase loss, reversal or imbalance; its LED indicates fault vs normal per the label on the relay.
likelyCauses: Rotation reversed at the unit disconnect
checks: Measure all three line voltages; swap two incoming leads if rotation is reversed (scroll compressors must rotate correctly)
Read the PMR label for LED meaning
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48/50TC IOM — phase monitor option (from memory; verify)

diagnosticTips: Sequence check: jumper R to G (fan), R to Y1 (compressor 1 + OFM), R to Y2 (compressor 2), R to W1 (IGC heat) at the low-voltage terminal board to isolate the thermostat from the unit.
The low-voltage terminal board (TB) is in the main control box; the 24 V transformer (TRAN) usually has a 208 and 230 primary tap — set it to the measured line voltage.

controls.name: Carrier / Bryant / Payne gas furnace control — two-digit amber LED status codes
controls.description: Furnace control board on Carrier/Bryant/Payne 58- and 59-series residential gas furnaces (59SC5A single-stage, 59TP6A/59TN6A/58CVA two-stage, 59MN7A modulating, 58SC0A, 58SU0A ultra-low-NOx). The amber LED flashes two-digit status codes: number of SHORT flashes = first digit, number of LONG flashes = second digit. Meanings are transcribed from the service labels printed in the Carrier troubleshooting guides 59MN7A-01T, TG-GFC80-02 and GFULN80-C-01TS and the 59SC5A-08SI label. Where boards differ (codes 21, 23, 31, 32, 43) the variants are given in the same entry. Code 44 does not appear in these four guides.
appliesTo: Bryant/Payne equivalents with the same board

faultCodes.meaning: NO PREVIOUS CODE – Stored status codes are erased automatically after 72 hours. After a component test, 11 means the inducer motor, gas valve and blower motor tested OK (59MN7A); on 2-stage boards (58CVA) it means the blower motor tested OK.
checks: After component test: visually check the hot surface igniter (and the inducer motor on 2-stage boards)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER ON AFTER POWER UP – (115 VAC or 24 VAC) – Normal operation. Blower runs for 90 seconds, if unit is powered up during a call for heat (R-W/W1 closed) or (R-W/W1 opens) during the blower on-delay period.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: LIMIT CIRCUIT LOCKOUT – Lockout occurs if the limit, draft safeguard, flame rollout, or blocked vent switch (if used) is open longer than 3 minutes or 10 successive limit trips occurred during high-heat (59MN7A: maximum-heat). Control will auto reset after 3 hours. Refer to status code #33.
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or restricted duct system
Restricted vent / improper vent sizing / excessive wind
Inadequate combustion air supply (flame rollout switch open)
checks: Rollout switch is manual reset: find the cause before resetting
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: IGNITION LOCKOUT – Control will auto reset after 3 hours. Refer to status code #34.
faultCodes.notes: 59SC5A label: failed to ignite and prove flame in 4 attempts.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR LOCKOUT – Indicates the blower failed to reach 250 RPM or the blower failed to communicate within 30 seconds after being turned ON in two successive heating cycles. Control will auto reset after 3 hours. Refer to status code #41.
checks: Check blower motor, blower wiring and furnace control (see 41)
faultCodes.notes: ECM / variable-speed boards (59MN7A, 58CVA, 59TP6A, 59TN6A).
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: GAS HEATING LOCKOUT – Control will NOT auto reset.
likelyCauses: Stuck closed gas valve relay on control
Miswire or short to gas valve wire (BLUE wire on 59MN7A)
58SU0A: 24 VAC sensed at the gas valve when it should not be present
checks: Check gas valve wiring for miswire or short
Replace the control if the valve relay is stuck
59SC5A label: turn off power and wait 5 minutes to retry
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: ABNORMAL FLAME-PROVING SIGNAL – Flame is proved while gas valve is de-energized. Inducer will run until fault is cleared.
checks: Shut gas off at the manual valve if flame persists
Replace the gas valve if it leaks through
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: PRESSURE SWITCH DID NOT OPEN. 58SU0A (transducer furnace): PRESSURE > 0.15 in. w.c. AT START-UP.
likelyCauses: 58SU0A: obstruction in pressure tubing or transducer vent holes, defective transducer, transducer wiring
checks: Check the switch opens with the inducer off
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: SECONDARY VOLTAGE FUSE IS OPEN
likelyCauses: Short circuit in secondary voltage (24 VAC) wiring including thermostat leads
checks: Disconnect thermostat leads to isolate the short circuit
Replace the fuse after the short is found
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: MODEL SELECTION OR SETUP ERROR – If status code 25 only flashes 4 times on power-up the control is missing its model plug PL4 and is defaulting to the model selection stored in memory. If 25 flashes continuously: model plug PL4 missing and no valid model stored in permanent memory (forgot to install PL4 on a service replacement control); thermostat call with setup switch SW1-1 ON; thermostat call with SW1-6 ON; SW1-1 and SW1-6 both ON together; two different furnace models twinned; service replacement control is incorrect (59MN7A needs a modulating board with software version V17 or later).
checks: See the rating plate / wiring diagram for the model plug number and resistance values
Move PL4 from the old board to a service replacement control
Return SW1-1 and SW1-6 to OFF after code recall / component test
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: 2-stage (58CVA, 59TP6A, 59TN6A): HIGH-HEAT PRESSURE SWITCH OR RELAY DID NOT CLOSE OR REOPENED – Control relay may be defective or gas valve is mis-wired. Refer to status code #32. 59MN7A modulating: MEDIUM PRESSURE SWITCH, HIGH PRESSURE SWITCH, OR PSR RELAY DID NOT CLOSE OR REOPENED. 59SC5A single-stage: LPS or HPS PRESSURE SWITCH DID NOT CLOSE OR REOPENED (HPS failing to close on 3 successive cycles = 3 h lockout). 58SU0A: PRESSURE TRANSDUCER INPUT DOES NOT SENSE TARGET PRESSURE OR PRESSURE IS OUT OF RANGE.
likelyCauses: Improper vent sizing / restricted vent / excessive wind
Air leak between vestibule and blower compartment
Low inlet gas pressure (if LGPS used)
Defective or mis-wired pressure switches / defective PSR relay
Plugged condensate drain; water in vent piping (sagging pipe)
Defective inducer or low inducer voltage (115 VAC)
checks: Check pressure-switch wiring and the PSR relay
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: LOW-HEAT (59MN7A: LOW) PRESSURE SWITCH DID NOT CLOSE OR REOPENED – Failed to close on a call for heat or opened during low/minimum heat. 2-stage: if open longer than five minutes, inducer shuts off for 15 minutes before retry. If opens during blower on-delay period, blower will come on for the selected blower off-delay. 59MN7A: if it opens within 5 minutes after ignition the next heating cycle is restricted to maximum-heat.
likelyCauses: Air leak between vestibule and blower compartment
Low inlet gas pressure (if LGPS used)
Water in vent piping, possible sagging pipe
Defective inducer motor or low inducer voltage (115 VAC)
checks: 59MN7A: if wind is the problem turn setup switch SW1-3 ON to boost inducer speed
Check condensate drain and vent pitch
Measure inducer voltage and the pressure switch make point
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: LIMIT CIRCUIT FAULT – Indicates the limit, draft safeguard, flame rollout, or blocked vent switch (if used) is open or the furnace is operating in high-heat only mode due to 2 successive low heat limit trips (59MN7A: maximum-heat only mode after 2 successive limit trips at any rate <= 71% of maximum). Blower will run for 4 minutes or until open switch remakes whichever is longer. If open longer than 3 minutes, code changes to lockout #13. If open less than 3 minutes status code #33 continues to flash until blower shuts off. Flame rollout switch requires manual reset.
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or restricted duct system
Inadequate combustion air supply (flame rollout switch open)
59MN7A: improper minimum- or maximum-heat gas input adjustment; improper limit switch or no limit gasket
checks: Check filter, duct restrictions and temperature rise
Find the cause of a rollout trip (blocked heat exchanger or vent) before resetting the manual-reset rollout switch
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: IGNITION PROVING FAILURE – Control will try three more times before lockout #14 occurs (58SU0A: ignition 4 times). If flame signal is lost during blower on-delay period, blower will come on for the selected blower off-delay.
likelyCauses: Gas valve defective or turned off
Inadequate flame carryover or rough ignition
checks: Clean the flame sensor with fine steel wool
Flame sense: 0.5 microamps DC minimum, 4.0-6.0 nominal (DC microammeter in series with the sensor wire)
Green/Yellow wire MUST be connected to furnace sheet metal
Check inlet gas pressure and that the manual valve is open
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: GAS VALVE FAULT – Indicates the modulating gas valve failed to respond to a command from the furnace control or power to the gas valve electronics was interrupted.
likelyCauses: Intermittent RED, YELLOW, or ORANGE wire at gas valve or PL8 connections
checks: Check the gas valve harness and PL8 connector
faultCodes.notes: 59MN7A modulating furnace.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR FAULT – Indicates the blower failed to reach 250 RPM or the blower failed to communicate within the prescribed time limits. Thirty seconds after being turned ON or ten seconds during steady-state operation. In the component test: blower motor failed test.
checks: Check blower, wiring, and furnace control
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: INDUCER MOTOR FAULT – Indicates the inducer has not started within 20 seconds after a call for heat, the inducer motor RPM is outside its valid range of operation, or the inducer RPM signal was lost for 5 seconds during operation.
likelyCauses: Blockage in the tubing to the pressure switch assembly or blockage in the pressure tap at the collector box
checks: Check inducer, wiring, and furnace control
faultCodes.notes: RPM-sensed inducers (59MN7A, 58SU0A).
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: LOW-HEAT PRESSURE SWITCH OPEN WHILE HIGH-HEAT PRESSURE SWITCH IS CLOSED (59MN7A: LOW OR MEDIUM PRESSURE SWITCH OPEN WHILE MEDIUM OR HIGH PRESSURE SWITCH IS CLOSED)
likelyCauses: Low inlet gas pressure (if LGPS used)
Low-heat (or medium) pressure switch stuck open
Water in vent piping, possible sagging pipe
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

faultCodes.meaning: CONTROL CIRCUITRY LOCKOUT – Auto-reset after 1 hour lockout due to: flame sense circuit failure; gas valve relay stuck open; software check error.
checks: Replace control if status code repeats
faultCodes.source: Carrier 59MN7A Troubleshooting Guide 59MN7A-01T, 'Service/Status Code Instructions' p.8; TG-GFC80-02 (58CVA/58CVX) p.6-7; GFULN80-C-01TS (58SU0A) p.6-7; 59SC5A-08SI service label

ledPatterns.meaning: CONTINUOUS OFF – Check for 115 VAC at L1 and L2, and 24 VAC at SEC-1 and SEC-2.
CONTINUOUS ON – Control has 24 VAC power.
RAPID FLASHING – Line voltage (115 VAC) polarity reversed.
checks: Check line-voltage polarity and furnace ground

diagnosticTips: Reading the code: short flashes = first digit, long flashes = second digit (e.g. 3 short + 4 long = 34).

Code recall: disconnect the R thermostat lead (or the ABCD connector on communicating boards), reset power, put setup switch SW1-1 ON. Clear history: SW1-1 ON and jumper R, W/W1 and Y/Y2 together until code 11 flashes. Return SW1-1 to OFF afterwards.
Component test: thermostat off / R removed, reset power, SW1-6 ON. Inducer runs the whole test; igniter and blower run 15 s each; then 11, 25, 35, 41 or 42 flashes. Return SW1-6 to OFF.
Stored codes are erased automatically after 72 hours. Lockouts 13, 14 and 15 auto-reset after 3 hours, 45 after 1 hour; 21 never auto-resets.
Flame sense: DC microammeter in series with the flame-sensor wire. Below 0.5 microamp is a failure; 4-6 microamps is typical (59MN7A-01T).
Limit codes: 33 escalates to 13 if the switch stays open more than 3 minutes. Two successive low-heat limit trips put a 2-stage furnace into high-heat-only mode. Rollout switches are manual reset.

controls.name: ICP *9MAC modulating furnace control (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite) — amber LED status codes
controls.description: Control board on ICP-brand *9MAC variable-speed modulating condensing furnaces. Status codes are a single or two-digit number: the first number is the count of SHORT flashes and the number after the (+) sign is the count of LONG flashes (e.g. 6+1). HEARTBEAT (bright-dim-bright-dim) is normal. Each ICP code corresponds to a Carrier two-digit code (given in notes). Transcribed from the ICP troubleshooting guide 440 08 4001 00 service label. Older ICP single-stage/two-stage boards are NOT covered: their single-digit tables come from secondary sites that conflict; read the door label.
appliesTo: *9MAC (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite)

faultCodes.meaning: PRESSURE SWITCH DID NOT OPEN
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 23.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: LOW PRESSURE SWITCH DID NOT CLOSE OR REOPENED – Indicates the low pressure switch input failed to close on a call for heat, or opened during minimum-heat. If opens during blower on-delay period, blower will come on for the selected blower off-delay. If opens within 5 minutes after ignition the next heating cycle will be restricted to maximum-heat.

Low inlet gas pressure (if LGPS used)

checks: If wind is the problem turn setup switch SW1-3 ON to boost inducer speed
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 32.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: LIMIT CIRCUIT FAULT – Indicates the limit, or flame rollout is open or the furnace is operating in maximum-heat only mode due to 2 successive limit trips while operating at any rate less than or equal to 71% of maximum rate. Blower will run at intermediate heat airflow for 4 minutes or until open switch remakes whichever is longer. If open longer than 3 minutes, code changes to lockout #7. Flame rollout switch requires manual reset.
likelyCauses: Improper minimum- or maximum-heat gas input adjustment
Dirty filter or restricted duct system
Improper limit switch or no limit gasket
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 33.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: ABNORMAL FLAME-PROVING SIGNAL – Flame is proved while gas valve is de-energized. Inducer will run until fault is cleared.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 22.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: IGNITION PROVING FAILURE – Control will try three more times before lockout #6 + 1 occurs. If flame signal is lost during blower on-delay period, blower will come on for the selected blower off-delay.
likelyCauses: Gas valve defective or turned off
Inadequate flame carryover or rough ignition
checks: Clean flame sensor with fine steel wool
Flame sense .5 micro amps DC min., 4.0-6.0 nominal
Green/Yellow wire MUST be connected to furnace sheet metal
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 34.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: LIMIT CIRCUIT LOCKOUT – Lockout occurs if the limit, or flame rollout switch is open longer than 3 minutes or 10 successive limit trips occurred during maximum-heat. Control will auto reset after 3 hours. Refer to status code #4.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 13.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: GAS HEATING LOCKOUT – Control will NOT auto reset.
likelyCauses: Stuck closed gas valve relay on control
Miswire or short to gas valve BLUE wire
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 21.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: MEDIUM PRESSURE SWITCH, HIGH PRESSURE SWITCH, OR PSR RELAY DID NOT CLOSE OR REOPENED – Indicates the medium or high pressure switch input failed to close on a call for intermediate- or maximum-heat, or opened during a heat cycle. PSR relay may be defective. Refer to status code #3.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 31.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: POLARITY – Check for correct line voltage polarity. If units are twinned, check for proper low-voltage (24V) transformer phasing.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier boards show this as rapid flashing.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER ON AFTER POWER UP – (115 VAC or 24 VAC) – Normal operation. Blower runs for 90 seconds, if unit is powered up during a call for heat (R-W/W1 closed) or (R-W/W1 opens) during the blower on-delay period.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 12.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR LOCKOUT – Indicates the blower failed to reach 250 RPM or the blower failed to communicate within 30 seconds after being turned ON in two successive heating cycles. Control will auto reset after 3 hours. Refer to status code #4 + 1.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 15.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: MODEL SELECTION OR SETUP ERROR – If status code 2 + 5 only flashes 4 times on power-up the control is missing its model plug PL4 and is defaulting to the model selection stored in memory. If it flashes continuously: model plug PL4 is missing and there is no valid model stored in permanent memory (forgot to install PL4 on a service replacement control); thermostat call with setup switch SW1-1 ON; thermostat call with SW1-6 ON; SW1-1 and SW1-6 both ON together; two different furnace models twinned; service replacement control is incorrect (need modulating board with software version V17 or later).
checks: See rating plate for model plug number and resistance values if code flashes continuously
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 25.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: GAS VALVE FAULT – Indicates the modulating gas valve failed to respond to a command from the furnace control or power to the gas valve electronics was interrupted.
likelyCauses: Intermittent RED, YELLOW, or ORANGE wire at gas valve or PL8 connections
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 35.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR FAULT – Indicates the blower failed to reach 250 RPM or the blower failed to communicate within the prescribed time limits. Thirty seconds after being turned ON or ten seconds during steady-state operation.
checks: Check blower, wiring, and furnace control
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 41.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: INDUCER MOTOR FAULT – Indicates the inducer has not started within 20 seconds after a call for heat, the inducer motor RPM is outside its valid range of operation, or the inducer RPM signal was lost for 5 seconds during operation.
likelyCauses: Blockage in the tubing to the pressure switch assembly or blockage in the pressure tap at the collector box
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 42.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: LOW OR MEDIUM PRESSURE SWITCH OPEN WHILE MEDIUM OR HIGH PRESSURE SWITCH IS CLOSED
likelyCauses: Low inlet gas pressure (if LGPS used)
Water in vent piping, possible sagging pipe
Low or Medium pressure switch stuck open
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 43.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

faultCodes.meaning: IGNITION LOCKOUT – Control will auto reset after 3 hours. Refer to status code #6.
faultCodes.notes: Carrier equivalent 14.
faultCodes.source: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace Troubleshooting Guide 440 08 4001 00, service label p.6-7

ledPatterns.meaning: HEARTBEAT – Control has 24 VAC power (normal). After a component test it means the inducer motor, gas valve and blower motor tested OK; visually check the hot surface igniter.

ON SOLID – The control is locked out and will auto reset after 1 hour. Lockout could be due to: flame sense circuit failure; gas valve relay stuck open; software check error. Reset power to clear lockout. Replace control if status code repeats.
checks: Check that the correct model plug PL4 is installed
Reset power; replace the control if it repeats

ledPatterns.meaning: CONTINUOUS OFF – Check 115 VAC at L1 and L2, 24 VAC at SEC-1 and SEC-2, and 24V fuse.

diagnosticTips: Reading the code: first number = short flashes, number after the + = long flashes (e.g. 6+1 = six short, one long). ICP has no code 11; a cleared history ends with the HEARTBEAT.
Component test: thermostat off / R removed, reset power, SW1-6 ON; inducer runs the whole test, igniter and blower 15 s each. Result: HEARTBEAT = OK, or 2+5, 3+5, 4+1, 4+2. Return SW1-6 to OFF.
A service replacement control needs the model plug PL4 moved from the old board; without it and with no valid model in memory the board shows 2+5 continuously.
Older ICP single-stage/two-stage boards use single-digit flash counts that are not in this table; secondary sources conflict, so read the door label.

sourceDocs.title: ICP *9MAC Variable Speed Modulating Condensing Furnace, Troubleshooting Guide

sources: ICP troubleshooting guide 440 08 4001 00 (*9MAC modulating), service label (shareddocs.com, read 2026-10-20)

controls.name: Carrier Infinity 2-stage outdoor unit control (25HNB6/25HNB9 heat pumps) — amber LED status codes
controls.description: Two-stage outdoor control on Infinity 25HNB6/25HNB9 heat pumps (Puron, 2-5 tons). The amber LED flashes the code number; codes also appear on the Infinity user interface. Only one code is displayed (the most recent, with the highest priority). Transcribed from Table 6 of the 25HNB6/25HNB9 installation instructions. The same table style is used on 25HNA and 24ANA two-stage units (not checked here).

faultCodes.meaning: System Communications Failure – Communication with User Interface lost. Check wiring to User Interface, indoor and outdoor units.
checks: Check ABCD wiring to the User Interface, indoor and outdoor units
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Invalid Model Plug – Control does not detect a model plug or detects an invalid model plug. Unit will not operate without correct model plug.
checks: Install the correct model plug (see the model plug table in the installation instructions)
An RCD replacement board has no model/serial data: move the model plug from the original board
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: High Pressure Switch Open – High-pressure switch trip. Check refrigerant charge, outdoor fan operation and coils for airflow restrictions.
checks: Check outdoor fan operation and outdoor coil (cooling) for airflow restrictions, or indoor airflow in heating
faultCodes.notes: Contactor de-energized, outdoor fan runs up to 15 min; contactor re-energizes after 15 min if demand remains and the switch has reset; restart attempted every 15 min. Cycling low voltage defeats the 15-min delay. 3 consecutive trips = 84.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Low Pressure Switch or Discharge Temp Switch Open – Low-pressure switch or discharge temperature switch trip. Check refrigerant charge and indoor air flow.
checks: Check indoor airflow (cooling), outdoor fan operation and outdoor coil (heating)
faultCodes.notes: Same 15-min sequence as 31. 3 consecutive trips = 83.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Control Fault – Outdoor unit control board has failed. Control board needs to be replaced.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Brown Out (230 v) – Line voltage < 187v for at least 4 seconds. Compressor and fan operation not allowed until voltage>190v. Verify line voltage.
faultCodes.notes: 5-minute compressor recycle delay after a brownout. Brown-out protection can be defeated for sites with noisy power using the forced-defrost pins. Some older secondary tables number this 47.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: No 230v at Unit – There is no 230v at the contactor when indoor unit is powered and cooling/heating demand exists. Verify the disconnect is closed and 230v wiring is connected to the unit.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor Air Temp Sensor Fault – Outdoor air sensor not reading or out of range. Ohm out sensor and check wiring.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault – Coil sensor not reading or out of range. Ohm out sensor and check wiring.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Thermistors out of range – Improper relationship between coil sensor and outdoor air sensor. Ohm out sensors and check wiring.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Low Stage Thermal Cutout – Compressor operation detected then disappears while low stage demand exists. Possible causes are internal compressor overload trip or start relay and capacitor held in circuit too long (if installed).
faultCodes.notes: Same 15-min sequence as 31. Repeats lead to 81.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: High Stage Thermal Cutout – Compressor operation detected then disappears while high stage demand exists. Possible causes are internal compressor overload trip or start relay and capacitor held in circuit too long (if installed).
faultCodes.notes: Repeats lead to 82.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Contactor Shorted – Compressor voltage sensed when no demand for compressor operation exists. Contactor may be stuck closed or there is a wiring error.
checks: Inspect the contactor for welded contacts
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: No 230V at Compressor – Compressor voltage not sensed when compressor should be starting. Contactor may be stuck open or there is a wiring error.
checks: Check wiring between contactor and compressor
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Low Stage Thermal Lockout – Thermal cutout occurs in three consecutive low/high stage cycles. Low stage locked out for 4 hours or until 24v power recycled.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: High Stage Thermal Lockout – Thermal cutout occurs in three consecutive high/low stage cycles. High stage locked out for 4 hours or until 24v power recycled.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: Low-Pressure Lockout – Low pressure switch trip has occurred during 3 consecutive cycles. Unit operation locked out for 4 hours or until 24v power recycled.
checks: Check refrigerant charge and indoor airflow (cooling); outdoor fan and outdoor coil (heating)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

faultCodes.meaning: High-Pressure Lockout – High pressure switch trip has occurred during 3 consecutive cycles. Unit operation locked out for 4 hours or until 24v power recycled.
checks: Check refrigerant charge, outdoor fan operation and outdoor coil (cooling) or indoor airflow (heating)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Infinity 2-Stage Heat Pump Installation Instructions, Table 6 – Troubleshooting (p.12-13)

ledPatterns.pattern: 25HNB amber LED on solid, no flash
ledPatterns.meaning: Standby – no call for unit operation (normal operation).
Low Stage Cool/Heat Operation (normal operation).
High Stage Cool/Heat Operation (normal operation).
Brown out protection is Disabled (Table 6; the text section of the same instructions says status 5 = brownout active and 6 = disabled — the document contradicts itself).
Brown out protection is Active (Table 6; the text section says 6 = disabled — the document contradicts itself).

diagnosticTips: Time delays: 5 min on a call for cooling/heating (bypass by momentarily shorting the Forced Defrost pins), 5 min compressor recycle after brownout, 1 min outdoor fan delay at the end of cooling when OAT >= 100 F, 20 s outdoor fan delay after defrost.

Defrost: interval 30/60/90/120 min or AUTO (Infinity UI overrides the DIP switches). Demand = coil <= 32 F for 4 min; terminates at 65 F coil or 10 min; at OAT <= 25 F defrost runs high stage and terminates at 50 F. Defrost only below 50 F OAT.
Charge in high stage only, by subcooling, with OAT 70-100 F and indoor 70-80 F; target subcooling is on the rating plate.
Model and serial numbers are stored on the board at the factory; an RCD replacement board has none, so the model plug must be moved from the original board.

controls.name: Carrier Infinity variable-speed outdoor control (24VNA6 AC / 25VNA4 HP, PCM + VFD) — BASE-EXPANSION fault codes
controls.description: Infinity Series variable-speed AC and heat pump with Greenspeed Intelligence (24VNA6 / 25VNA4, 2-5 tons). The PCM reports codes to the thermostat as BASE-EXPANSION (e.g. 33-15). For each base code Table 6 gives a 'Fault' expansion (limiting or temporary shutdown) and a 'Malfunction' expansion (the escalated lockout). Meanings are the Table 6 descriptions; notes come from the code descriptions in the same service manual. The PCM has a scrolling matrix display (up to 4 active codes, highest priority first), a status light, comm light and VFD comm light.

faultCodes.meaning: Line Voltage Low (fault)
checks: Check line voltage at the terminal block and tighten line connections
Line voltage is measured on the 24 V transformer secondary with a factory scaler: after replacing the PCM or the transformer, recalibrate line voltage with the service app or nuisance trips occur
faultCodes.notes: Set when line < 180 VAC RMS at any time, or < 185 VAC for more than 5 s; clears above 187 V. Unit will not run. Does not escalate to a malfunction.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Line Voltage High (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Set above 285 VAC at any time or above 280 VAC for more than 5 s.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: PCM-Bluetooth Module Communication Failure (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Bluetooth module (BTM) not communicating with the PCM.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor Coil Freeze Protection (fault)
likelyCauses: Low indoor airflow (dirty filter, restrictive ductwork)
checks: Check filter and external static pressure
faultCodes.notes: Compressor speed is reduced as saturated suction approaches 32 F.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: 5V PCM External Power Out of Range (malfunction / lockout)
checks: Unplug the PCM-VFD harness and measure pin 3 (GND) to pin 4 (+5 VDC) at the VFD end
If 5 V is present reconnect and power-cycle; if the fault remains replace the VFD
If 5 V is missing unplug sensors one at a time (a shorted transducer harness can pull it down); if still absent replace the PCM
faultCodes.notes: The PCM supplies 5 VDC to the VFD (pin 4 of the 6-pin harness) and to the pressure transducers.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Invalid Model Plug (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.notes: Model plug (two resistors) does not match any model in the variable-speed software.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Model Plug Missing (fault)
checks: Power down, install the correct plug, re-power (the PCM ignores a plug installed while powered)
faultCodes.notes: Plug missing but a valid model is stored in memory; unit runs.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Model Plug Missing (malfunction / lockout)
checks: Power down, install the correct plug, re-power
faultCodes.notes: No plug and no valid model in memory; unit will not run.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Model Plug Changed (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Installed plug differs from the stored value.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: VFD/Equipment Model Mismatch (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.notes: Model plug not compatible with the installed VFD (described as 'VFD System Lockout - Model Mismatch').
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: PCM MCU Old Version (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Board must not be used; return it for warranty.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: PCM Reprogramming Failure (fault)
checks: Check PCM software against the latest version; reprogram via the Infinity control or the Carrier Service Tech App
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: EEPROM Write Failure (fault)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Fuse 1 Open (PEV / RVS) (malfunction / lockout)
checks: Look for a short in the PEV, RVS or Bluetooth module harness
faultCodes.notes: Fuse 1 powers the PEV, reversing valve solenoid and Bluetooth module. AC units may still run if the differential is under 100 psi; heat pumps will not run.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Fuse 2 Open (LLV) (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.notes: Fuse 2 powers only the field-installed liquid line solenoid; system will not run.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor High Pressure Limit (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Discharge-transducer limit varies with model and speed; the system limits speed, and restarts after a 5-min delay with a reduced maximum speed each time.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor High Pressure Limit (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: High Pressure Switch Trip (fault)
faultCodes.notes: 670 psi high pressure switch wired to the VFD (the transducer limit normally acts first); a broken or shorted HPS harness also triggers it.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: High Pressure Disable (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Discharge pressure too high to start (620 psig).
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor Low Pressure Limit (fault)
checks: Check liquid-line pressure drop at the condenser and at the evaporator
faultCodes.notes: Soft limit may be exceeded for up to 2 min, hard limit trips immediately (typical 30 psi and 15 psi); 4 occurrences = 32-55 and 2-h lockout.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor Low Pressure Limit (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Low Pressure Disable (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.notes: Suction too low to start safely; most likely a refrigerant leak.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor Low Discharge Limit (fault)
faultCodes.notes: 5-ton model only. 6 occurrences of 33-15 within 2 hours result in 33-55 and a 2-hour lockout.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor Low Discharge Limit (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor High Temperature Limit (fault)
faultCodes.notes: Discharge temperature > 230 F near the compressor; each event cuts next-start capacity by 25%; lockout when already at minimum capacity.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor High Temperature Limit (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor High Compression Limit (fault)
faultCodes.notes: High compression-ratio boundary; 2-h shutdown when already at minimum capacity.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor High Compression Limit (malfunction / lockout)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 24VNA6/25VNA4 Service Manual 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, Table 6 'Fault Code Table' p.25-26 and code descriptions p.15-24

checks: Read the active code on the PCM matrix display or thermostat

diagnosticTips: Diagnostic Code Recall: power off, jumper the Forced Defrost (J3) pins, power on; RECALL scrolls the most recent highest-priority codes from the last 240 h.
Shorting J3 for 1 s with the compressor off overrides the compressor protect delay ('OVERRIDE' scrolls); 5 s in heating forces a defrost.
The Carrier Service Tech App connects through the Bluetooth module: it reads codes and updates software.
PEV = Pressure Equalization Valve (24 VAC solenoid that equalizes suction/discharge before a start), not an expansion valve. PEV failure shows as 38-18, not as 33-15/33-55.
After replacing the PCM or the 24 V transformer, recalibrate line voltage with the service app or 14-94 / 15-94 nuisance faults occur.

controls.name: Carrier PIC II / PIC III (CVC / ICVC) chiller controls — STATE alarm and alert numbers (19XR, 19XRV, older 23XRV)
controls.description: Product Integrated Control generations II and III with the CVC/ICVC display on 19XR/19XRV centrifugal chillers (HFC-134a) and older 23XRV screw chillers. Alarms and alerts are numbered STATE codes: 100-111 prestart alerts (delay start only), 120-128 run capacity limited, 140-170 alerts, 200-259 and 282-286 protective limits (shutdown, manual reset), 260-271 sensor faults. Codes and messages are from the PIC III table (19XRV-CLT-7SS Table 16). PIC II with constant-speed ISM starters uses the same structure but numbers 200-227 mean different things (e.g. 200/201 = 1M/2M aux contact faults, 217 = motor overload trip 'Check ISM configurations'); confirm the controller generation before quoting a 200-series number. These numbers are NOT the PIC 5 ALM/ALT numbers.

diagnosticTips: Prestart alerts 100-111 only delay the start; start continues when the condition is corrected, no reset needed.
101 high bearing temperature: check oil heater, oil level, partially closed oil supply valves, clogged oil filters.
110/111 rectifier/inverter temperature: check that the VFD refrigerant isolation valves are open, plus the cooling solenoid and strainer.

Table 16 also maps PowerFlex VFD fault codes to ICVC states (e.g. VFD 200-201 Inverter Dsat -> 286; 216 Rectifier Ground -> 220; 222 High AC Line -> 211; 223 Low DC Bus -> 215; 225 Input Amp imbalance -> 209; 239 Power Phased ACB -> 206, swap two input phases).
PIC II (constant-speed ISM) and PIC III (VFD) use different meanings for 200-227: check 19XR-6SS for ISM machines.

controls.name: Carrier PIC 5 / PIC 6 chiller controls (19XR, 19XRV, 19DV AquaEdge) — ALM / ALT codes
controls.description: PIC 5 / PIC 5+ (10.4 in. touch screen, IOB boards, ISM or VFD, LEN bus) and PIC 6 on 19XR/19XRV centrifugal chillers and the 19DV two-stage centrifugal (R-1233zd(E)). Alarms are ALM-2xx (sensor faults, prestart failures, protective limits), ALM-3xx (communication), ALM-4xx (ISM / VFD faults), ALM-5xx (19DV Danfoss VFD faults); alerts are ALT-1xx. Alerts do not shut the machine down and reset automatically when the condition clears. Codes 200-453 and the ALT list are from the 19XR PIC 5 v3.3 manual (19XR-CLT-3T Tables 17/18; reset type parsed from the table layout). Additional codes are from the 19DV PIC6 manual (19DV-CLT-3T Tables 15/16), whose table notes it 'is not specific to 19DV'. PIC 6 v2.0 on 19XR (19XR-CLT-5T) uses the same numbers; differences from PIC 5 were not checked. These are NOT the PIC II/III STATE numbers.

diagnosticTips: The Reset Alarms menu shows up to 5 active codes (19DV: up to 10 current alarms/alerts; alarm history keeps the last 50).
Some ISM alarms are 'Swift Restart eligible' when the Auto Restart option is enabled.
Sensor alarms (ALM-200 to ALM-228) auto-reset; check that the IOB channel DIP switch (SW2) matches the sensor type (5K/10K thermistor or 100-ohm RTD).
ALM-254 low evaporator refrigerant temperature can be caused by condenser water entering the wrong (top) pass: reversed flow stacks refrigerant in the condenser.
ALM-257 high condenser temperature is NOT caused by the high-pressure switch (that is ALM-283).
ALM-262 condenser frozen can happen with the chiller off and brine below 32 F in the cooler.

controls.name: Carrier 30XA AquaForce (US) Navigator / scrolling-marquee alarm codes — PREFIX.SUFFIX
controls.description: US-built 30XA080-500 AquaForce air-cooled screw chillers with the Navigator / ComfortLink-style display. Alarms show as PREFIX.SUFFIX with an alarm number: A1/B1/C1 compressor failure (alarm 111-xx, 112-xx, 113-xx), Co communication, FC factory configuration, MC master chiller configuration, P process, Pr pressure transducer, Sr service notification, th thermistor. Transcribed from 30XA-6T Table 61; each meaning gives the description, trip criterion, control action and reset type. EU-built 30XA/30XW with the Touch Pilot screen use numeric codes instead (touch-pilot-30xa-30xw).

diagnosticTips: HPS trips (A1/B1/C1.03) need the reset button on the high pressure switch pressed as well as a control reset.
Phase loss .06-.08 trips on more than 48% current imbalance.
Y-delta failure .10: delta current not 25% above wye current; check the delta contactor.
Contactor failure .11 / unable to stop .12: more than 15% of MTA current 10 s after the stop command means a welded contactor; on .11 the oil solenoid stays energized.
CPM DIP switch S1 must match the factory MTA, otherwise .15/.16.
Thermistor range for all th alarms is -40 to 245 F; transducer alarms trip at 0 vdc or SST > EWT with EXV < 50% for 1 minute.

controls.name: Carrier Touch Pilot (EU 30XA/XAS/XB/XBP/XW AquaForce) — numeric alarm codes
controls.description: Touch Pilot control (Pro-Dialog successor) on EU-built 30XA/30XAS/30XB/30XBP/30XW AquaForce screw chillers, incl. PUREtec R-1234ze(E) versions. Codes show in the Reset Alarms menu; the Current Alarm menu and histories show the text. Families: 150xx thermistors, 120xx transducers, 4xxx communication, 100xx process, 13-nnn maintenance, 57xxx EXV, 55001/56001 software, 7001/8000/9001 configuration, 11nn/21nn/31nn compressor A/B/C faults (meanings match the 30XA-6T .01-.19 suffixes; the board is called TCPM), 20-nnn ... 44-nnn variable-speed drive errors and alerts (nnn = Danfoss drive code). Transcribed from the Touch Pilot manual 13453 section 8.6.

diagnosticTips: Pump faults 10032/10033 swap to the standby pump.
Low suction, customer interlock and flow switch faults reset automatically for the first alarm in 24 h, then need a manual reset; low oil level allows three automatic resets in 24 h.
Compressor code = circuit digit (1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C) + 1 + two-digit fault, e.g. 1105 = compressor A locked rotor, 2103 = compressor B high-pressure protection.
Drive codes: the number before the dash locates the drive (20/23/26 = circuit A/B/C controller error; 38/41/44 = alerts), the nnn after it is the Danfoss alarm number.

controls.name: Danfoss VLT drive alarm / alert numbers on Carrier AquaForce chillers (Touch Pilot 20-nnn ... 44-nnn)
controls.description: Danfoss VLT variable-speed drive (variator) codes as listed in the Carrier Touch Pilot manual 13453 section 8.6.2. The chiller shows a drive fault as XX-nnn: 20/23/26-nnn = variable speed controller error circuit A/B/C (units without option 17), 20-25-nnn = fan drives A1-A3/B1-B3 with option 17, 38-44-nnn = drive alerts. nnn is the drive number below. The manual lists only the most common alarms; refer to the Danfoss documentation for others. Each entry gives the alarm and/or alert text and Carrier's action. 30XV uses 17nnn/18nnn (compressor VFD) and 20nnn-25nnn (fan VFD) with the same drive codes.

controls.name: Carrier PIC6.1 / Carrier Controller (30XV AquaForce PLUS) — numeric alarm codes
controls.description: Carrier PIC6.1 touch-screen controller (software v9.x) on 30XV140-500 Series B variable-speed air-cooled screw chillers with Greenspeed. Uses the Touch Pilot numbering, extended with compressor VFD codes 17nnn/18nnn (failure) and 35nnn/36nnn (warning), fan VFD codes 20nnn-25nnn, EC fan codes 26znn-28znn and 59000-61012 diagnostics. Codes shared with Touch Pilot carry the same meaning. Transcribed from the 30XV-6T alarm list.

faultCodes.meaning: Circ A - Loss of Refrigerant Flow. Trips when either condition occurs 3 times within 24 h: (1) (Approach > Approach High Threshold OR SST < Freeze - SST Low Offset) AND DGT Rate > DGT Rate Threshold AND startup timer elapsed; or (2) DGT > DGT High Threshold AND SST Rate < SST Rate Threshold. Circuit shut down and not allowed to start for 5 min; automatic reset.
likelyCauses: Loss of refrigerant flow (charge or EXV)
faultCodes.notes: Override 66 is activated.
faultCodes.source: Carrier AquaForce PLUS 30XV140-500 Controls, Start-Up, Operation, Service and Troubleshooting 30XV-6T (PIC6.1 / Carrier Controller), alarm list

faultCodes.notes: Override 66 is activated.

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A - saturated suction Temperature out of MAP compressor. Circuit shut down; manual reset.

diagnosticTips: 10123/10124 IM PM motor mismatch: the unit configuration does not match the compressor motor type (induction vs permanent magnet); check it after a compressor or drive replacement.
61005-61012: a drive was turned off from its LCP keypad; put the drive back in remote/auto.
10087/10088 loss of refrigerant flow locks the circuit out for 5 minutes per trip (3 times in 24 h).
10101/10102: SST above MOP 62.6 F for an accumulated 90 minutes.

controls.description: US 30RB060-390 AquaSnap air-cooled scroll chillers (Greenspeed 080-390). Alarms show as PREFIX.SUFFIX: A1-A4/B1-B4/C1-C4 compressor (SPM scroll protection module), Co communication, Ct welded contactor, FC/MC configuration, P process, Pr pressure transducer, Sr service, th thermistor, V0/V1/V2 variable-speed fan drive.
