sequenceOfOperation: Cooling, electromechanical: thermostat closes R-G (IFC energizes IFM) and R-Y1; 24 V passes through the circuit-1 safety string (HPS, LPS, FPT, CLO contact) to C1, starting compressor 1 and the OFM. On two-stage units R-Y2 energizes C2 (compressor 2) the same way. Opening of any safety drops C and, on CLO-equipped units, latches the compressor off until Y is removed.

Cooling with economizer: with outdoor air suitable (Free Cool LED / W7220 'economizing'), Y1 first modulates the outdoor-air damper between minimum position and full open to hold the mixed-air setpoint (~50-55 °F); mechanical cooling is added (Y1/Y2 passed to compressors) only when free cooling cannot satisfy or when outdoor air is not suitable. On DDC units (RTU Open/SystemVu) the controller stages compressors and drives the damper itself.

Heating (gas): thermostat closes R-W1. The IGC verifies the limit and rollout switches are closed, starts the IDM, proves the draft pressure switch, energizes the spark igniter and opens the gas valve; flame must be sensed within the trial period or the IGC retries and eventually locks out (LED 5 flashes). The IGC energizes the IFM ~45 s after ignition. W2 opens the second stage of the two-stage gas valve on medium/high-heat units. When W drops out the gas valve closes, IDM post-purges and the IFM runs ~45 s more.
Heating (electric heat on 50-series): W1/W2 energize the heater contactors through the heater's own limit switches; the IFM runs with G or through the heater relay.
Heat pump (50TCQ/HCQ): O/B reversing valve energized in cooling on Carrier (verify on diagram); defrost is time/temperature initiated by the defrost board.
notes: Designators and sequence are the standard Carrier light-commercial rooftop legend, largely from memory of the 48/50TC IOM; a verifier confirmed CLO (Compressor Lockout, factory option or accessory), FPT (Freeze-Up Protection Thermostat), IFC, OFC, PMR, IGC and TRAN against 48TC/48TF legend excerpts and the CLO reset behaviour against Carrier TIP05-002. 'LAS' (low-ambient switch) was not found on any 48/50TC legend and was removed. Treat the rest as low-confidence and confirm on the unit's own wiring diagram (inside the control-box door).

Phase monitor: a factory option on 48/50TC 3-phase units; SystemVu units report a phase-monitor trip as F206 (48/50FC-GC-01T). Scroll compressors run backwards (noisy, no pumping) if rotation is reversed — check on start-up.
Single-phase (voltage code 3 / Bryant J) sizes 04-07 use a PSC/ECM IFM and capacitor-start compressor; there is no PMR.

Newer (2023+) builds add a Low Pressure Switch bypass timer and, on R-454B (48/50JC) units, refrigerant detection sensors (RDS) that force the IFM on and lock out ignition/compressors on a leak alarm.
sources: Carrier 48/50TC Installation Instructions (48TC-8-16-02SI, 48TC-14-xxSI and successors) — wiring diagram legend and Sequence of Operation (mostly from memory; CLO/FPT/IFC/OFC/PMR/IGC/TRAN confirmed by a verifier against 48TC/48TF legend excerpts)
Carrier TIP05-002 — compressor lockout (CLO) reset behaviour

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat cycles on limit / IGC shows 2 or 4 flashes; supply air very hot
likelyCauses: Low airflow: loaded filters, slipping or broken belt, blower wheel dirty, IFM on wrong speed tap or wrong drive setting
Over-fired: manifold pressure high or wrong orifices for altitude/gas
checks: Measure temperature rise (supply − return) and compare to the nameplate range
Check belt tension/condition and blower rotation; measure external static
Check manifold pressure (natural gas: 3.5 in. w.c. high fire / 1.7 in. w.c. low fire per the 48TC*D08 IOM; see nameplate)
sources: Carrier 48TC*D08 Installation Instructions — gas manifold pressure 3.5 in. wg high fire / 1.7 in. wg low fire (natural gas)

commonIssues.symptom: No heat, IGC LED 5 flashes (ignition lockout) — especially first cold snap of the season
likelyCauses: Gas pressure low (regulator, closed valve) or gas valve not energized
Spiders/debris in burners causing poor carryover
checks: Watch the trial: spark present? gas valve 24 V? flame lit then dropped (sensor) or never lit (gas/igniter)?
Clean the flame sensor with fine abrasive pad and re-check flame current
Verify inlet pressure under load and manifold pressure

commonIssues.symptom: Heat works, but indoor fan will not shut off or will not start in heating (cooling fan OK)
likelyCauses: IGC board fan relay contacts welded or failed (widely reported field pattern; no Carrier bulletin found — unverified)
IGC 1-flash modified delay after limit trips
checks: With no calls, check for 24 V on the IGC fan output; if present with W off, replace IGC
Check limit history (2/4 flashes) and airflow before replacing the board

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor won't run; 24 V present at Y but contactor coil dead (CLO tripped)
likelyCauses: HPS trip: dirty condenser coil, OFM/capacitor failed, overcharge
LPS trip: low charge, iced evaporator, low ambient without low-ambient control
checks: Remove the Y call to reset CLO, then watch pressures at restart
Check OFM runs and condenser coil is clean; check subcooling/superheat
Check FPT continuity with the coil warm

commonIssues.symptom: 3-phase scroll compressor loud, low amps, no pressure differential after install or after a power outage/utility work
checks: Check phase sequence at the unit; swap two incoming leads at the disconnect only
Verify all three line voltages under load and imbalance < 2 %
On units with PMR/F206, read the phase monitor LED

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer damper stuck open or never opens; high humidity / high indoor temp; iced evaporator in winter
likelyCauses: W7212 EconoMi$er IV: failed C7400 enthalpy sensor, failed actuator, minimum-position pot mis-set
W7220 EconoMi$er X: missing/failed S-bus OAT sensor (no free cooling), actuator alarms, MAT sensor error
Broken damper linkage / seized damper blades
checks: Command the damper open/closed (W7220 CHECKOUT menu, or 2-10 VDC test on W7212) and watch travel
Check 24 VAC at the actuator and the 2-10 VDC / S-bus signals
Inspect linkage and blade seals; verify minimum position with the fan running

commonIssues.symptom: Water in the unit / condensate overflow or drain pan not draining
likelyCauses: No trap or wrong trap depth on the drain (draw-through evaporator is under negative pressure)
checks: Verify a properly sized trap per the IOM (deeper than the fan's negative static in in. w.c.)
Clear and flush the drain; check the pan drains with the blower running

commonIssues.symptom: Belt-drive blower: squeal on start, low airflow, high supply temperature rise; frequent belt replacement
likelyCauses: Belt tension / worn or misaligned pulleys
Motor pulley set for wrong RPM (variable-pitch pulley)
checks: Check belt deflection and pulley alignment; check pulley groove wear with a gauge
Measure IFM amps vs FLA and external static; adjust pulley per the fan performance table

commonIssues.symptom: Humidi-MiZer unit: poor dehumidification, or cooling weak with the reheat coil hot
likelyCauses: Humidi-MiZer 3-way solenoid valve stuck in the reheat position, or CLV / RLV / LDV (cooling liquid / reheat liquid / liquid diverter) valves not shifting between normal cooling, subcooling (Reheat1) and hot-gas reheat (Reheat2) modes
CRC (cooling relay / Humidi-MiZer control relay) or humidistat / DDC dehumidify input wiring
checks: Verify the dehumidify input state and 24 V at the CRC relay and the 3-way solenoid / CLV / RLV / LDV valve coils in each mode (48-50TCHC-01XA troubleshooting)
Compare liquid-line and reheat-coil temperatures in normal cooling — reheat coil should be near liquid temperature when not in reheat
sources: Carrier Humidi-MiZer Adaptive Dehumidification System for 48/50TC, HC — Installation / Troubleshooting (48-50TCHC-01XA); 48/50HC 04-28 controls manual Humidi-MiZer section (Reheat1 subcooling / Reheat2 hot-gas reheat modes)

commonIssues.symptom: SystemVu/RTU Open unit runs but BAS shows sensor alarms; readings drift from measured values
likelyCauses: Thermistor wiring shared with line-voltage conduit (induced noise)
SAT sensor mounted too close to the heat exchanger / in radiant view
checks: Compare the controller reading to a calibrated probe at the sensor location; reseat plugs
Relocate SAT downstream per the IOM if it reads high with heat on

commonIssues.symptom: Legacy R-22 rooftop (48HJ/TJ/TM/TF): repeat compressor failures / slugging
likelyCauses: Refrigerant migration on long off cycles (no crankcase heater on many small sizes)
Overcharged after retrofit to an R-22 replacement blend
TXV flooding from a loose/insulated-badly bulb
checks: Check superheat at the compressor after 10 min run; confirm bulb mounting
Weigh in the charge per nameplate when a retrofit refrigerant is used; confirm the refrigerant on the retrofit sticker

commonIssues.symptom: Unit dead, no 24 V: transformer secondary fuse/CB open
likelyCauses: Shorted contactor coil or economizer actuator
TRAN wired to wrong primary tap (208 vs 230) overheating
checks: Isolate: disconnect the field thermostat wires at TB; if the fuse holds, the short is in the field wiring
Ohm contactor coils and check the economizer 24 V load
Verify the transformer tap matches measured line voltage

commonIssues.symptom: Gas furnace limit trips: code 33 (limit circuit fault) then 13 (limit circuit lockout, 3 h)
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or restricted duct system
Restricted or undersized vent, excessive wind
59MN7A: improper minimum/maximum gas input adjustment, wrong limit switch or missing limit gasket
checks: Check filter, duct restrictions and temperature rise
Rollout switches are manual reset: find the cause (blocked heat exchanger or vent) before resetting
Two successive low-heat limit trips put a 2-stage furnace into high-heat-only mode
sources: Carrier 59MN7A-01T and TG-GFC80-02 service labels (codes 13/33)
Carrier 59SC5A-08SI service label

commonIssues.symptom: Gas furnace will not prove flame: code 34 (ignition proving failure) then 14 (ignition lockout, 3 h)
likelyCauses: Low inlet gas pressure or manual valve shut
Defective hot surface igniter or gas valve
Poor control ground continuity (green/yellow wire not on sheet metal)
checks: Measure flame current with a DC microammeter in series with the sensor wire: below 0.5 microamp is a failure, 4-6 microamps typical
Clean the flame sensor with fine steel wool
Check inlet gas pressure and furnace ground
sources: Carrier 59MN7A-01T troubleshooting guide (flame sense 0.5 to 6.0 microamps, typical 4-6)
Carrier TG-GFC80-02 service label (code 34)

commonIssues.symptom: Condensing gas furnace pressure switch codes 31/32 (switch did not close or reopened)
likelyCauses: Plugged condensate drain or water in the vent (sagging pipe)
Restricted or undersized vent, excessive wind
Air leak between vestibule and blower compartment
Low inducer voltage or defective inducer
Low inlet gas pressure (if LGPS used)
checks: Clear the condensate trap and drain; check vent pitch
Check pressure tubing and switch wiring
59MN7A: if wind is the cause turn SW1-3 ON to boost inducer speed
sources: Carrier 59MN7A-01T service label (codes 31/32)
Carrier 59SC5A-08SI service label (code 31)

commonIssues.symptom: Infinity 2-stage heat pump (25HNB) locks out on pressure: 31/32 trips leading to 84/83
likelyCauses: Outdoor fan failure or outdoor coil blocked (cooling)
Low indoor airflow (heating for HPS; cooling for LPS)
checks: After a trip the outdoor fan runs 15 min; the compressor restarts after 15 min if the switch has reset
3 consecutive trips lock the unit out for 4 hours or until 24 V is recycled
Check charge by subcooling in high stage only (OAT 70-100 F, indoor 70-80 F)
sources: Carrier 25HNB6/25HNB9 Installation Instructions, Table 6 and pressure-switch sequence

commonIssues.symptom: Infinity variable-speed (24VNA6/25VNA4) nuisance 14-94 / 15-94 line voltage faults after a board or transformer replacement
likelyCauses: Line voltage is measured on the 24 V transformer secondary with a factory scaler; after replacing the PCM or the transformer the scaler is wrong
checks: Recalibrate line voltage with the Carrier service app
Measure line voltage at the terminal block and tighten line connections
sources: Carrier 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, codes 14-94 / 15-94

commonIssues.symptom: Infinity variable-speed (24VNA6/25VNA4) will not start: 38-18 High Differential Pressure Start Disable
likelyCauses: Non-functioning PEV (pressure equalization valve): mechanical failure
PEV coil not mounted on the valve body
PEV coil or harness failure (Fuse 1 also feeds the PEV: see 28-71)
checks: Confirm the coil is on the PEV body
Replace the harness and coil first, then the PEV body
PEV is not an expansion valve; 33-15/33-55 low discharge is a different fault (reversing valve, charge, TXV/EXV, compressor)
sources: Carrier 24VNA6-25VNA4-1SM, codes 38-18 and 33-15/33-55

commonIssues.symptom: Infinity variable-speed gen 1 (24VNA0/25VNA0) compressor temperature lockout: repeated 59 events then 85
checks: Check airflow and the TXV; replace the filter drier
Scroll thermistor about 10 kohm between scroll and common terminals
85 is a 240-minute lockout; 88 is the inverter temperature lockout (repeated 75), not the scroll temperature path
sources: Carrier 24VNA0-25VNA0-1SM flash-code tables (codes 59, 85, 88)

commonIssues.symptom: 30XA compressor high-pressure trip (A1/B1/C1.03, Touch Pilot 1103/2103/3103) will not reset
likelyCauses: Loss of condenser airflow, fouled coil or condenser water problem
checks: Press the reset button on the high pressure switch, then reset the alarm at the control
sources: Carrier 30XA-6T Table 61 (.03)
Carrier Touch Pilot 13453 section 8.6.3

commonIssues.symptom: 30XV will not run after a compressor or drive replacement: 10123/10124 IM PM motor mismatch
likelyCauses: Unit configuration does not match the compressor motor type (standard induction vs permanent magnet)
checks: Set the configuration to the installed motor type
Also check that drives are not left off at the LCP keypad (61005-61012)

commonIssues.symptom: 30RB compressor not started or pressure not established (P.16-P.27)
likelyCauses: No power to the compressor or faulty contactor
checks: Check phase rotation (P.28 = improper phasing seen by the reverse rotation board)
sources: Carrier 30RB-8T Table 47

commonIssues.symptom: 19XR (PIC 5) low evaporator refrigerant temperature trips (ALM-254) with normal charge
likelyCauses: Condenser water piped to enter the wrong (top) pass: reversed flow stacks refrigerant in the condenser
Float valve or liquid line isolation valve
Division plate gasket bypass, fouled tubes
checks: Verify condenser water enters the bottom row first
Check float valve, liquid isolation valve and evaporator transducer
sources: Carrier 19XR-CLT-3T Table 17 (ALM-254)

notes: Brands: Carrier, Bryant, Payne (same factories, same WWYY serial style, Bryant/Payne have their own model nomenclature); ICP brands (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite, Airquest) share ownership and use a YEAR-FIRST (YYWW) serial with their own nomenclature.

Nameplate reading: Carrier commercial rooftop plates list MODEL NO., SERIAL NO., electrical data (volts/phase/Hz, MCA, MOP, compressor RLA/LRA, fan FLA), refrigerant and charge per circuit, and test pressures. Decode only the MODEL NO. line; ETO / 'Product No.' strings are not the model.

Light-commercial model layout (48/50TC, HC, LC, FC, GC, KC, JC, FE): 12 characters, dash, 5 option characters. Positions: 1-2 unit type, 3-4 series, 5 heat size, 6 refrigeration-system/cooling-stage option, 7-8 size code, 9 sensor options, 10 indoor fan static option, 11 design revision, 12 voltage; after the dash: base-unit controls, intake/exhaust, packaging & seismic, electrical options, service options (after-dash order consistent with catalog models but not yet read off the nomenclature page).

Refrigerants: 48/50TC/HC/LC/FC/GC/KC, 38AU, 40RU, 38AP, 30RAP/30RB, 48/50A2-A5, P, N = R-410A (Puron); legacy HJ/TJ/TM/TF/EJ, AJ-AY, Z, 30RA, 09DK = R-22 (verify retrofit sticker); 48/50FE and 48/50JC (2025+) = R-454B (A2L, Puron Advance) — confirm on plate.

Open verification items after the 2026-09-26 review: read the after-dash position order off the 48TC-7-16-03PD nomenclature page; read the 48/50FE nomenclature page (48-50FE-8-16-01PD) and the position-6 refrigeration-system letters; confirm whether Bryant 582K/559K pair with Carrier 48/50FC/GC/KC; Carrier Style-3 (1980-88) serial month map; the Carrier 1960s-70s week + year-letter serial style (single source); ComfortLink A150 on rooftop tables; RTU Open full alarm-point names.

2026-10-20 pass (from knowledge/carrier research with downloaded Carrier PDFs): added residential furnace LED codes (Carrier/Bryant/Payne two-digit, ICP *9MAC x+y), Infinity 2-stage 25HNB, Infinity variable-speed 24VNA6/25VNA4 (BASE-EXPANSION) and gen-1 24VNA0/25VNA0 codes; chiller controls PIC II/III, PIC 5/PIC 6 (19XR/19DV), 23XRV PIC6, 30XA Navigator, Touch Pilot, Danfoss VLT drive codes, 30XV PIC6.1 and 30RB; residential model formats 24VNA6/25VNA4, 24VNA9/25VNA8, 24ACC4, 59/58 furnaces, 58CVA; Carrier serial plant letters E/X.

Correction applied (24VNA0/25VNA0): persistent code 59 'Compressor Scroll Temp Out of Range' escalates to 85 COMPRESSOR TEMP LOCKOUT, not 88 (88 = INVERTER TEMP LOCKOUT), per 24VNA0-25VNA0-1SM; an earlier secondary excerpt said 88.

Correction applied (24VNA6/25VNA4): the 'non-functioning PEV' text belongs to 38-18 High Differential Pressure Start Disable, not to 33-15/33-55. PEV = Pressure Equalization Valve (not an expansion valve). 33-15/33-55 causes per the service manual: malfunctioning reversing valve, low charge, missing or stuck TXV/EXV, compressor not operating properly.

Chiller alarm numbering differs by controller: PIC II (constant-speed ISM) and PIC III (VFD) give different meanings to STATE 200-227; PIC II/III STATE numbers are not PIC 5 ALM/ALT numbers; 23XRV PIC6 uses its own ALM/ALT list. Touch Pilot XX-03 is printed with the XX-02 text but is the high-pressure-switch alarm (30XA-6T .03).

Not covered: Carrier ductless (Midea-built) and VRF (Toshiba-Carrier) error codes, Infinity Touch / Cor / Evolution UI screens, non-communicating heat pump defrost boards, older ICP single-digit furnace boards, i-Vu / Open controllers, SmartVu; 30XA-7T, 30XW-5T, 30RC, 30MP, 30RAP-8T and 30G/H alarm tables were downloaded but not parsed; chiller and Bryant/ICP residential nomenclature not decoded.
